questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation worked example, which segment carries the mandatory primary balancing label?
options: Company
Account
Future
Cost Center
questions.explain: The Company segment carries the primary balancing label, with one value per legal entity (1000 for the US parent, 2000 for the Canadian subsidiary).

questions.q: Why does the Intercompany segment's value set mirror the Company segment's values exactly?
options: It is a coincidence with no functional purpose
Because intercompany tracking is about identifying which other entity a transaction is really with, consistent with the restriction covered in Lesson 21
Because Oracle Fusion requires all segments to share identical value sets
Because the Cost Center segment also requires this mirroring
questions.explain: The Intercompany segment's values must mirror the primary balancing segment's values, since it identifies the specific trading entity involved.

questions.q: Why was a Product Line segment deliberately left out of the worked design, even though LTV Manufacturing makes more than one product?
options: Because the Future segment already contains product data
Because Oracle Fusion does not support product-related segments
Because the business does not yet need product-level financial reporting, consistent with the 'simplest structure that satisfies today's requirements' principle
Because Product Line segments are always illegal in a chart of accounts
questions.explain: The design follows Lesson 5's guiding principle: build the simplest structure that satisfies real, current requirements, not a hypothetical future one.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the unlabeled 'Future' segment in the worked design?
options: It replaces the need for cross-validation rules
It automatically becomes the primary balancing segment
It has no purpose and could be removed with no effect
It is reserved so that a genuinely new reporting need later can be added by populating its value set, without redesigning the chart of accounts structure from scratch
questions.explain: Reserving an unlabeled segment lets the company add a real future requirement (like a product line) without the costly, disruptive process of redesigning the structure itself.

questions.q: Which fictional company does this lesson use for its worked chart of accounts example, and why is it significant?
options: A random, unnamed company with no later relevance
LTV Manufacturing Corporation, the same fictional company used later in this path's capstone project
A real, named Fortune 500 manufacturer
OracleERPGuide, the practice environment provider
questions.explain: LTV Manufacturing Corporation is explicitly the same fictional company students will revisit in the capstone project later in the path.
